text:
maya (support): FYI ACME reported big embedding p95 regressions after our maintenance window (eu-west-1). They see median ~200ms but p95 jumped from ~1s to 6-8s since ~2026-03-15 02:10 UTC. request_id: req_32a9b6

acme-sre (customer): yes, started ~02:10. We pinned timestamps to specific calls — see traces. This is customer-impacting on production dedicated pool.

maya (support): customer says model=embed-xlarge, route=dedicated-eu-west1-poolB, concurrency=16. They attached a sample failing curl and a trace id.

acme-sre (customer): repro curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -d '{"model":"embed-xlarge","input":"test"}'` — trace shows long server-side queue and occasional 504s.

sam (oncall): I'm pulling infra metrics now. Initial look: host-side nvme io wait increases correlated with the spikes. p95 network is fine, CPU low, but NVMe wait time and iowait jump around.

nora (infra): We had a coordinated driver+firmware rollout in eu-west-1 at 01:45-02:05 UTC (deploy job: deploy/ew1-gpu-driver-2026-03-15-01). ops-bot: can you confirm which hosts got firmware bump?

ops-bot: rollout record: deploy/ew1-gpu-driver-2026-03-15-01 applied to poolB nodes: gw-045, gw-046, gw-049, gw-052. GPU firmware updated on gw-046, gw-049.

liam (eng-sre): Noted. We've seen similar patterns where firmware+driver changes interact with host kernel NVMe scheduling and cause intermittent host io stalls under KV-cache pressure. Could be request sequencing + prefix KV cache hitting NVMe hotspots.

sam (oncall): quick repro script I used to spike: loop 1000 curl requests with concurrency 40 to embed-xlarge on poolB. Observed queue depth on NVMe controller jump >200 and read_lat p95 spike to 30ms -> causing overall inference p95 to climb. Snippet:
```
# repro (internal)
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-xlarge","input":"hello"}' &
  if (( i % 40 == 0 )); then wait; fi
done
```

nora (infra): logs from gw-049 NVMe controller: `nvme_io_wait=480ms, qdepth=220` around 02:13. Kernel dmesg shows `blk_mq: timeout` warnings on some hosts.

acme-sre (customer): we also see transient auth 502s but main issue is latency. Is there a suggested mitigation short-term?

liam (eng-sre): Short-term mitigations: 1) Reduce max concurrency on that route to 8 via routing config to reduce concurrent KV cache pressure. 2) Route heavy embed traffic to fallback pool that wasn't updated (poolA). 3) Disable background flush that touches cold KV pages (we can throttle background IO).

nora (infra): I can temporarily add an iptables/driver-level qdisc rate limit for host background IO on gw-049/gw-046, but that's fussy. Easier: mark gw-046 and gw-049 as draining from poolB and shift traffic. Starting now.

ops-bot: action: mark-draining poolB: gw-046 gw-049 (initiated by nora). ETA shift ~40s.

maya (support): telling ACME we will shift their traffic and reduce concurrency. Will ask them to validate.

acme-sre (customer): after shifting, p95 improved to ~1.2s within 2 minutes. Still a few tails at ~2s but much better. Thank you.

liam (eng-sre): Good. For root cause: we need to bisect driver/firmware vs kernel change. Recent kernel backports were also merged in earlier that day (kernel: 6.5.4-backport-rt). Possible three-way interaction: CUDA/driver, GPU firmware, blk_mq scheduling.

sam (oncall): Next steps: 1) Collect full iostat/blktrace from affected hosts for 02:00-02:30 window (nora to grab). 2) Reproduce in staging by applying same driver+firmware to 2 nodes and run KV-heavy workload (liam + infra). 3) If repro, plan immediate rollback of firmware on affected hosts (nora to coordinate).

nora (infra): I've pulled iostat and blktrace and uploaded to /internal/incidents/1776543210/artifacts.tar.gz. Also snapshot of kernel logs.

liam (eng-sre): For staging repro, use the following sequence to mimic KV cache pressure: 1) load ~50k unique prefix requests to populate cold KV, 2) run embed concurrency 32 for 5 minutes, 3) monitor `nvme qdepth` and `blk_mq` counters. I'll run this in staging-rlc.

maya (support): ACME asked about workaround to avoid future regressions: can we add route preference override in their API keys to always go to poolA?

liam (eng-sre): Yes — we can add a policy tag on their API key: `preferred_pool: poolA` until fix is deployed. I'll prepare a short config change and feature flag to revert when safe.

acme-sre (customer): appreciated. Please keep us posted. We had business reports queued for the morning.

sam (oncall): Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1776543210. Assigning to eng-sre and infra. Will schedule postmortem after RCA.

liam (eng-sre): If staging repro is successful we'll try a targeted driver rollback vs kernel rollback. Rolling back firmware is heavier — prefer to roll driver first if that repros.

nora (infra): I'll prepare rollback playbook and safety checklist (rollback-driver.sh, firmware-recovery.md).

maya (support): ACME acknowledged mitigation and will validate tomorrow AM. I'll update ticket and close when they confirm stable.

ops-bot: note: scheduled maintenance windows for next week in eu-west-1 — we'll pause any fleet-wide firmware rollouts until RCA.

sam (oncall): thanks all. tagging hardware and kernel teams for visibility. Will update channel when we have staging results.

liam (eng-sre): tl;dr: driver+firmware update exposed a host-kernel NVMe scheduling regression under KV-cache heavy traffic. Mitigation: drain affected hosts, reduce concurrency, route to unaffected pool, and repro in staging. Root-cause investigation ongoing.
